page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression rated in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by middle-50% rankings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth also performs within the average tier, reaching 75.86 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 55.65 GB/sec for large-block writes.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.sn2.3xlarge is its modest single-threaded performance compared to its multi-threaded capacity. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio offer stable, predictable resource density for multi-threaded workloads without the premium of high-frequency compute-optimized or memory-optimized classes. It is suitable for workloads such as static web serving, Redis database operations, and moderate multi-threaded application hosting, but less optimal for single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference.
